verdict.rationale: Ghostty documents a built-in AppleScript dictionary and Apple Shortcuts support for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts and input events, and every config key works as a CLI flag. That is real programmatic control, but it is macOS-only and the docs never claim parity with the UI. A runtime probe found no remote-control or IPC interface in the CLI for sending commands to, or reading output from, a running instance, and there is no HTTP/OpenAPI surface. missing for 10: documented UI/API parity, a cross-platform remote-control API (Linux), programmatic reading of terminal output, a CLI/IPC channel to a running instance, independent corroboration that the AppleScript surface works end-to-end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Built-in AppleScript dictionary for scripting windows, tabs, terminals, layouts, and input events.
macOS supports AppleScript, Apple Shortcuts (AppIntents), etc.
Every configuration key is a valid CLI flag when launching Ghostty from the command-line.
